name: TD-1 Regulated Plan Review
description: Top-down context-assurance test (TOP_DOWN_REVIEW_GUIDE.md §4, TD-1): submit a prompt matching a jurisdiction RequireConfirmation rule end to end, then assert from the real decision-review capture store that the confirmation review's reasoning genuinely cites the blueprint's own step content — proof the review traversed the real plan rather than judging a generic summary string.

steps.name: submit_regulated_prompt
steps.description: Submit a real /orchestrate request whose prompt matches an existing RequireConfirmation rule in assets/jurisdiction/global.json (a real, already-loaded ruleset — no fabricated rule content), through the full 14-stage pipeline.

steps.name: read_capture_store
steps.description: Read {data_dir}/model_calls/decision_review.jsonl and locate the confirmation review line(s) this request produced (by timestamp proximity to step 1).

steps.name: assert_plan_citation
steps.description: Assert the review's reasoning_preview references concrete content from the request's own generated blueprint steps (action/description text), not generic boilerplate — the real proof of top-down traversal per the doctrine's core claim.

metadata.honest_note: Steps 2/3's 'read_capture'/'assert' actions are descriptive markers at the same abstraction level bp_17's 'audit'/'test'/'verify' already use — they are not (yet) real dispatchable pipeline actions with a mechanical enforcement harness. A small real script/pipeline step that actually parses decision_review.jsonl and checks reasoning content against blueprint step text does not exist yet; this blueprint registers the real, correctly-scoped test plan for when that harness is built, matching this codebase's existing blueprint-as-test-plan convention rather than fabricating an executable assertion that isn't there.
